answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may submit jobs, then slash that bond if independent auditors confirm fraud. The bond links reputation to costly capital: making a thousand fake agents requires funding a thousand locks, not merely generating names, and splitting work across them does not erase the exposure. A bridge can relay audit proofs across markets, while zephyr might name a low-volume test period; at the nadir of trust, honest agents still have reason to audit because valid challenges earn part of the slash.
